l.i: nà sumpsisset, suadebat homini socer, ut
vir quidam à Bethlehema Iudæa, orta in
finibus illis fame profectus est ad peregri-
nandum in agrū Moabiticum, unà cum
sua coniuge, duobusq; filiis. Viri nomen e-
ex Bethlehema Iudæae. His in agrum
duob. filiis superstitibus. Filii uxores Moa-
bitidas duxerunt, quarū uni Orpha, alte-
ri Rhuta nomen fuit: atq; illic circiter de-
duobus natis & viro superstes, cum apud
bus, in Iudæam reverti contendit, easq;

page.notes: The first line of text is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Doubtful: the sign after "Revertimini" at the right end of the last line is a small mark I could not identify, so I have not transcribed it. The word after "levasse" is partly obscured by a ligature and I read it as "levasse". The "LXXIII." is a bare number and is written as a paragraph, not a heading, per the rules.
